recipes.name: Green Bean Casserole Remix
ingredients_raw: 2 (9 ounce) packages frozen cut green beans, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place green beans into a 1 quart or similar sized casserole dish.

Fry bacon in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat until browned and crispy. Remove to drain on paper towels. Drain off some of the grease, leaving enough to coat the bottom of the pan. Add mushrooms to the grease in the pan and season with garlic powder and onion powder. Cook and stir until tender, about 4 minutes.

Pour the half-and-half into the pan with the mushrooms and stir to scrape the bacon flavor from the bottom of the pan. Simmer until thickened slightly, about 5 minutes. Pour this mixture over the green beans. Crumble bacon over the top and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake for 20 minutes in the preheated oven, or until the sauce is bubbling and the top is toasted.

raw_recipe.headline: Green Bean Casserole Remix
raw_recipe.description: Welcome to a new and tastier version of the classic green bean casserole with crispy bacon, fresh mushrooms, garlic, cream, and Parmesan cheese.

review.reviewBody: So I have been making this for awhile now and after this thanksgiving had to give it a review. I was trying to use fresh green beans, and although the cream of mushroom came out fabulously well, the green beans never cooked all the way and it was watery. So this time I sweated some onions and garlic in a good amount of butter, then I added the green beans and sauteed until good and done. Think canned french cut as an example. This removed a lot of the liquid. I used tongs to move the green beans from my pan to the casserole dish so that there was no excess liquid. But don't throw it away! I used it in the cream of mushroom which I made with heavy cream instead, and used a corn starch/water mixture to thicken. It came out PERFECT! And was sooo good and got plenty of compliments. :)

I scaled this recipe in half which called for 5 slices of bacon. I used only 3, and that was plenty for us. I know there were reviewers who said it turned out watery. I have to wonder if they didn’t thaw the frozen green beans or didn’t thicken the half-and-half. But I found this a bit on the dry side. I think one of the most important ingredients in this casserole is the half-and-half, and I think more is needed. If I were to make this again, I’d increase the half-and-half, stir in the parmesan as well as the salt and pepper, and cook it down until it starts to thicken. It turned out OK, but I think with a few tweaks, the flavor could be greatly improved.

I was eager to try this recipe because I prefer not to cook with canned soup. I made as instructed (the magazine version) except did add cornstarch to the cream sauce based on others' comments. I tasted the cream sauce while it was cooking and it was amazingly delicious. But after baking, the sauce became watery, not a sauce at all, and did not cling to the green beans. I wonder if this is due to water cooking out of the frozen green beans? This recipe had so much promise and was so disappointing.

Stop reading now if you don't like changes - this is for my own memory more than anything!

Thanksgiving 2020:

This was really good with a few changes I made - I used up some fresh green beans that I pre-cooked. I used cream of onion rather than cream of mushroom - that's ALWAYS a great substitution, but it's darn hard to find. I order a 12 pack case from Amazon probably once a year. Good in ALL casseroles. I subbed in a bit of evaporated milk rather than using cream. I topped it with a mix of panko, butter and freshly grated parmesan cheese, and some onion and garlic powder. Very good even as leftovers!
Made it for athanksgiving dinner. Everyone loved it.
This recipe was a big hit at my family Christmas dinner. I added some bacon to the recipe and it was so tasty.
The bacon makes it wonderful. My family ask for this one.

This recipe was great! The bacon really added some needed flavor. I made a double batch (fresh green beans make a real difference), so I ended up making more of the sauce by using twice the liquid - 1/2 half & half and 1/2 chicken stock. I also thickened it with cornstarch as others had suggested. Added french fried onions on top as a salute to the traditional style. Will make again..thanks for this recipe!
Will it make it again. Tasty and easy.

This is a great base recipe. We can not eat mushrooms so I made celery soup (from this site). I only used 3 slices bacon and with the soup mixed it in the green beans. I did not add the cream as it was enough liquid in the bowl. I did put French onions on top. It was a great hit with everyone.
